question: Is the bound sized to guarantee a fit (UTF-8 bytes, since a BPE token always covers at least one byte, set under the 400,000-token window, which also cuts the tails of the 12 stored book-length pages between 259k and 786k characters that fit today), or sized to ordinary prose (characters, about a million, which leaves those 12 whole but can still overflow on pages like ascii.rest)?
answer: Size it in UTF-8 bytes under the window, 350,000 bytes for the 400,000-token openai/gpt-5.4-nano both production services run, because a byte bound is the only one that cannot overflow for any text, while its cost is a recorded tail cut on 8 of 39,022 stored items (each still sends about 60k words) and a character bound leaves a failure class that retries every cycle.
